## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The `--json` parser treats the next argument as its path even when that argument is another flag, so the advertised use of `--json` alongside `--junit` fails when `--json` comes first. Fix this before merging.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `--json` option to `parse_args` that defaults to `results.json` or takes an explicit path. It also adds `write_reports`, which writes each parsed report to its destination, and new tests in `tests/test_cli.py`.

(none)

## Important
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — Don't consume a following flag as the --json path — `parse_args(["--json", "--junit", "out.xml"])` stores `"--junit"` as the JSON path and then raises `unknown option: out.xml`. The `--json` branch takes `args[i + 1]` without the `startswith("--")` check that the `--junit` branch uses at line 7. — Users who put `--json` before `--junit` get an error, and `["--json", "--junit"]` writes a file named `--junit`. — Fix: Use the default when `args[i + 1].startswith("--")` and advance `i` only when a path is consumed, then add the `["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]` case to `test_json_default_and_explicit_path`.
